comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, women represented 27.9% of global employees and 25.3% of technical positions, while underrepresented minorities comprised 17.8% of US employees and 8.7% of US senior leadership positions.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose specific demographic compositions for their workforces or leadership bodies regarding gender and ethnicity. MU reports self-identified race and gender composition specifically for its Board of Directors (5 men, 4 women; 1 Asian, 1 African-American, 7 White), whereas INTC reports similar demographic metrics (27.9% women, 17.8% underrepresented minorities) for its broader global employee base and senior leadership. Both disclosures provide granular breakdowns of diversity statistics within the Human Capital section.

comparisons.peer_topic: Diversity and Inclusion Strategy and Initiatives
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA is committed to creating an inclusive culture and building a diverse talent pipeline, particularly for women and underrepresented minorities in technology. To achieve this, the company partners with diverse institutions, embeds recruiting teams, supports women's leadership development, provides executive sponsors, trains managers on diversity, and tracks metrics on retention, pay, and engagement.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA articulate a commitment to diversity and inclusion, with NVDA explicitly listing progress on diversity metrics as a key initiative. MU's disclosure provides static headcounts of diverse members on its Board of Directors, while NVDA details strategic efforts to build a diverse talent pipeline for women and underrepresented minorities, including supporting women's leadership development and training managers on diversity. Both topics fall under the management of human capital diversity.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm focuses DEI efforts on inspiring innovation through inclusive culture, recruiting diverse talent, and identifying strategic partners, supported by global employee network groups and engagement with diverse communities.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM disclose commitments to an inclusive and diverse workforce. MU demonstrates this through the specific ethnic and gender composition of its Board of Directors, while QCOM describes its strategic focus on inspiring innovation through an inclusive culture, expanding recruitment of diverse talent, and maintaining employee network groups for women and underrepresented populations. Both disclosures address diversity as a core component of their organizational structure.

sentences.text: Our Board of Directors was comprised of five men and four women as of August 29, 2024.
In addition, as of August 29, 2024, based on self-identification, one member of our Board of Directors is Asian, one member is African-American, and seven members are White.
We believe that a diverse workforce is important to our success, and we continue to focus on making Qualcomm a great place to work for everyone, including women and underrepresented populations.

Our recent efforts have been focused in three areas: inspiring innovation through an inclusive and diverse culture; expanding our efforts to recruit world-class diverse talent; and identifying strategic partners to accelerate our programs.

We have employee networks that enhance our inclusive and diverse culture, including global network groups focused on supporting women, LGBTQ+ employees and employees with disabilities, in addition to U.S.-based employee networks that focus on Asian American and Pacific Islander employees, Black and African American employees, Hispanic and Latinx employees and U.S. military members and veterans.
